entries.cue: Clear water pitcher inside a transparent toy cell model with a conspicuous outer rim.
entries.cue_scope: Inside/intra plus cell plus fluid tokens
entries.prior: New composition using docs/visual-cue-catalog.json#water-pitcher and a newly recorded generic cell-model ingredient; not a new fluid primitive.
entries.reason: Simple inside relationship is sufficient once cell identity is taught. Pitcher is a mnemonic prop, not intracellular anatomy, a distribution diagram, membrane behavior or a fluid instruction.

entries.cue: Same clear water pitcher outside the same transparent toy cell model, with a visible gap from its rim.
entries.cue_scope: Outside/extra plus cell plus fluid tokens
entries.prior: New contrast composition using docs/visual-cue-catalog.json#water-pitcher and the cell model from intracellular fluid in this bank.
entries.reason: Preserves the shared family cue while changing location only. Cell identity needs lesson context; no claim about actual compartment dimensions, body-fluid volumes, transport or membrane permeability.

No economical association proposed in this pass. Do not force an unfamiliar name or mole/syllable puzzle, or substitute a clinical calculation. Provisional hold, not evidence that no useful cue exists.

entries.cue: Dry shriveled sponge beside an almost empty water bottle.
entries.reason: Reuses existing dryness/depleted-water cue without equating dehydration and hypovolemia. Not diagnosis from appearance, measured deficit, a fluid choice or a treatment instruction.

entries.cue: Only a few salt crystals remain in a large transparent container.
entries.reason: Established learned depleted-container family; capacity/reference must be taught so sparse contents are not merely a serving. Not dietary causation, actual sodium concentration, volume status, a threshold or treatment.

entries.cue: Salt crystals visibly overflowing a transparent container.
entries.reason: Reuses established identity/excess relationship. Salt is a learned token, not a statement of cause, serum concentration, volume status or a dietary recommendation.

entries.cue: Only a few bananas remain in a large transparent container.
entries.reason: Keeps established potassium family; learned reference capacity is needed to distinguish depletion from a small serving. Not dietary causation, a laboratory value or potassium replacement advice.
Preserves the user's existing overflow cue rather than inventing a new hyperkalemia image. No dietary causation, serum value, threshold or treatment instruction.

entries.cue: Only a few horseshoe magnets remain in a large transparent container.
entries.cue_scope: Magnesium name token plus depleted-state association
entries.reason: Preserves mag-/magnet family with taught reference capacity. No claim magnesium attracts metal, or that visible quantity establishes deficiency, a threshold or replacement need.

entries.cue: Horseshoe magnets visibly overflowing a transparent container.
entries.cue_scope: Magnesium name token plus excess-state association
entries.reason: Established magnet/excess composition, not new discovery. Not a magnetic-property, laboratory concentration, cause or management claim.

entries.cue: Only a few bone-shaped tokens remain in a large transparent container.
entries.reason: Reuses calcium family without broken-bone imagery. Taught reference capacity matters; no claim of fracture, bone disease, serum value or need for calcium replacement.

entries.cue: Bone-shaped tokens visibly overflowing a transparent container.
entries.reason: Keeps the existing identity/excess family. Not anatomical bone growth, a serum measurement, cause, diagnostic criterion or treatment claim.

entries.cue: Bored-looking diner pushing away a plain bowl of bland soup.
entries.prior: new_chapter_record; familiar insipid/bland relationship, not a newly invented primitive
entries.reason: Economical partial-name association if the learner knows insipid. Soup refusal may instead mean dislike, so the name bridge must be taught. Not an observation about urine, a taste test, a symptom, dietary cause or a diabetes comparison.

entries.cue: Familiar matchbox with a few unlit matches beside it.
entries.prior: new_chapter_record; newly recorded matchbox family token, not a proprietary design or established catalog primitive
entries.reason: Familiar object can serve as a taught identity association without a pronunciation puzzle. Not a claim about the composition of every match, elemental phosphorus as a body-fluid species, chemical equivalence, combustion, laboratory values or treatment. Keep unlit and separate from sulfur/rotten-eggs primitive.

entries.cue: Only a few unlit matchbox tokens remain in a large transparent container.
entries.cue_scope: Phosph- family token plus depleted state
entries.prior: New composition using phosphorus matchbox token introduced in this bank and the catalog's established depleted-container relationship; not a second new primitive.
entries.reason: Shares learned phosph- family rather than inventing phosphate syllables. Full phosphate-related word needs lesson context; not equivalence of phosphorus and phosphate, serum concentration, dietary or replacement advice. Reference capacity must distinguish depletion from a small serving.

entries.cue: Unlit matchbox tokens visibly overflowing a transparent container.
entries.cue_scope: Phosph- family token plus excess state
entries.prior: New contrast composition using phosphorus matchbox token introduced in this bank and the catalog's established overflow relationship; not a new primitive.
entries.reason: Same phosph- identity and container family as the deficit counterpart. Not a claim of chemical equivalence, actual measured phosphorus or phosphate, mechanism, cause, diet or treatment. Collision with matches/fire requires taught lesson context; no flame or sulfur/stink cue added.
